lead: Phoenix gets little rain, but monsoon storms, slab leaks and AC overflows still cause plenty of water damage. DryFlare helps homes and businesses across the Valley dry out fast.
risk: monsoon flash floods, slab leaks and AC condensate overflows
risk_short: monsoon storms, slab leaks, AC leaks
why: The monsoon runs from mid-June through September. Storms build in the afternoon, drop heavy rain on hard desert ground and send water across streets and into homes. On September 8, 2014, Phoenix set a one-day rain record that flooded Interstate 10 and many neighborhoods.

Flat roofs with parapets are common, and clogged scuppers turn a storm into a ceiling leak. Hard water wears out water heaters and fittings early. Most homes sit on slabs, so pinhole leaks under the floor can go unnoticed. Attic air handlers drip condensate all summer; a clogged line soaks ceilings below.
image_alt: Ceiling drywall collapsed after a monsoon roof leak in a Phoenix home
image_caption: Clogged roof drains during a monsoon storm are a top cause of ceiling damage in Phoenix.
problems: Homes near washes and low streets
Older homes in Arcadia, Encanto and Maryvale
tips: Clear roof scuppers and drains before monsoon season.
Flush the AC condensate line with vinegar each spring.
Replace water heater supply lines every few years because of hard water.
Watch for warm floor spots or a jump in your water bill.
areas: Calls come from Downtown, Arcadia, the Biltmore, Ahwatukee, North Phoenix, Maryvale and Desert Ridge, plus Scottsdale, Tempe, Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert, Glendale and Peoria.

faq.q: Does monsoon flooding in Phoenix count as flood for insurance?
faq.a: Water that flows across the ground into your home is usually treated as flood, which needs a separate flood policy. Rain that comes through a storm-damaged roof is often covered by homeowners insurance.
